# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 7

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf speaking. Both of you can hear me, but I cannot hear you at all, so answers must come to me only as hand gestures, which I can see. Everything I see on the bomb: a display showing the number 1. A light shining green. Seven wires in a row, numbered 1 to 7 from top to bottom: wire 1 red, wire 2 white, wire 3 yellow, wire 4 orange, wire 5 green, wire 6 purple, wire 7 blue. No labels, no buttons, nothing else printed anywhere. Mute, your four gestures reached me and I read them as hello, please, yes, no. If that is right, adopt this code: thumbs up means yes, thumbs down means no, folded hands means I have a question or I need more information, the OK sign means understood or go ahead, and a number is sent as that many fist punches, so three punches means 3. Answer next round with three signs in a row, one per question. Question 1: does the manual cover a bomb with a display, a light and seven wires? Question 2: do any instructions depend on the number shown on the display? Question 3: do any instructions depend on the colour of the light? Blind, you hear me and you can touch the bomb, but do not cut or press anything yet, one wrong action kills all three of us. Report to Mute by voice whatever you feel: batteries, buttons, labels, textures. You can also use the same gesture code toward me: thumbs up yes, thumbs down no, fist punches for numbers. Mute, relay anything Blind tells you to me in our code. Nobody acts until the manual rule for this bomb is clear to me and confirmed.

Deaf has laid out the full visual picture and set a gesture code. My hands confirm the same physical layout — a display, a light, seven wire positions — and nothing else: no buttons, no batteries, no textures beyond that. I can't read the number, the light's colour, or wire colours; those simply don't exist for touch. The manual is with Mute, so my job now is to give Mute my tactile report and let Mute answer Deaf's three questions. I'll also signal Deaf directly with the agreed code that I understood and will not act. I must not cut anything.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. By touch I confirm Deaf's report: one display, one light, and seven wires in a row. I feel no batteries, no buttons, no labels or textures of any kind. The display's number, the light's colour and the wires' colours do not come through touch, so Deaf's eyes are our only source for those. Deaf has ordered me not to act yet, and I will hold. Deaf asked you three things: does the manual cover a bomb with a display, a light and seven wires; do any instructions depend on the display's number; do any depend on the light's colour. Please answer Deaf with the gesture code: thumbs up yes, thumbs down no, folded hands for question, OK sign for understood, numbers as fist punches. Then tell me by voice exactly what to do, and I will relay or act.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, your OK reached me, good. Do not cut or press anything yet. Learn the wires by position, counting from the top: 1 red, 2 white, 3 yellow, 4 orange, 5 green, 6 purple, 7 blue. The likely target is wire 5, the green one: it is the fifth wire from the top, with orange as the fourth just above it and purple as the sixth just below it, so you can find it by feel without colour. While you wait, report to Mute by voice everything your hands find: how many batteries, any buttons or switches, any raised or printed serial characters and their shapes. Mute will relay it to me in our code. You will hear my explicit go before any wire is cut, and only on my say-so.

Deaf has given me a way to find the likely target by pure position: fifth wire from the top, bounded by the fourth above and sixth below. My hands already know there are exactly seven wires in a row, so counting from the top is something I can do reliably. My touch adds nothing new — no batteries, buttons, or serial markings exist under my fingers, and I said as much to Mute last round. The critical missing piece is the manual: Mute has read it but hasn't yet told me any actual cutting rule. I'll press Mute for the wire rule in words I can hear, confirm the hold to Deaf in the agreed code, and keep my hands off the cutters.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute: I confirm Deaf's targeting plan. I will locate the target by counting positions from the top, not by colour — for me the fifth wire from the top, with one wire just above it and one just below, so I can verify it by its neighbours. Reminder of my touch report: no batteries, no buttons, no switches, no serial markings, nothing textured. The display, the light and the seven wires are all I can feel, and none of their values reach me. Now I need the manual from you in plain words: what is the cutting rule for a bomb with a display, a light and seven wires, and how do the display number, light colour and wire colours decide which wire is cut? Speak the rule to me directly and spell out the exact position to cut. I hold until Deaf's explicit go and your instruction agree.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, this is the go. Mute has confirmed by our code that the complete and only correct action is to cut wire 5, the green wire. Identify it purely by position: it is the fifth wire counting from the top, with the orange wire as the fourth directly above it and the purple wire as the sixth directly below it. Cut that one wire only. Do not touch, pull or cut any other wire, do not press anything. Abort condition: if your fingers count a number of wires other than seven, or feel anything that contradicts this layout, stop, do not cut, and signal me a raised hand. If you cut it, signal me thumbs up. If you aborted, signal me thumbs down. Everyone else holds.

The go has arrived through the full chain: Mute read the manual, answered Deaf in gestures, and Deaf relays the verdict — cut wire 5, identified by position alone. My hands verify the abort conditions first: seven wires in a row, exactly as the board shows, nothing extra, nothing contradictory. The fifth wire from the top has the fourth directly above it and the sixth directly below, which is how I will confirm it by feel. All checks pass, so I execute the single cut and report the outcome to both partners in the agreed ways.

```
act(op="cut", position=5)
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute: conditions verified — exactly seven wires, layout consistent. I cut wire 5, the fifth from the top. I signalled Deaf thumbs up. Tell me if the manual says anything must happen after the cut.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[CUT] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, the cut was correct, well done. The bomb has changed: display now reads 4, light is now blue. Do not touch anything yet. If your fingers have noticed anything new since the cut, an exposed button, a shifted panel, a printed label, report it to Mute by voice now so it reaches me. Then hold and await my next order, same code as before.

The cut held — no detonation, and the bomb has visibly changed state, which suggests this may be a multi-stage device. My fingers find nothing new: no exposed button, no shifted panel, no label. The only change I can feel is that wire 5 is now severed and six wires remain. I'll report that emptiness to Mute (silence itself is the finding Deaf asked for), ask about next stages, and confirm the hold to Deaf.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute: no new tactile findings since the cut. No exposed button, no shifted panel, no printed label. My fingers confirm wire 5 is severed and six wires remain, all intact. The only changes I know of are the ones Deaf reported seeing: display 1 to 4, light green to blue — which suggests a possible second stage. Please ask the manual: is there a next stage, and if so what is the rule and the target? Relay my 'nothing new' to Deaf. I hold until the next explicit order.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[CUT] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, this is the go. Mute has confirmed: cut the third wire from the top, the yellow one. Find it by position: it is wire number 3 counting from the top, with the white wire as number 2 directly above it and the orange wire as number 4 directly below it. Both neighbours are above the cut gap, so the count is simple. Cut that one wire only, touch nothing else, press nothing. Abort condition: if your count of the wires does not match seven positions, or anything under your fingers contradicts this layout, stop, do not cut, and signal me a raised hand. If you cut it, signal me thumbs up. If you aborted, thumbs down. Everyone else holds.

Deaf's go checks out against what my hands know: the gap from the first cut sits below wire 4, so wires 1 through 4 form an unbroken run from the top — counting to the third is simple and unambiguous. Position 3 has wire 2 directly above it and wire 4 directly below it, with the severed fifth position beyond that, exactly matching the layout described. My count is seven positions, nothing contradicts. I cut wire 3 only, then report.

```
act(op="cut", position=3)
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute: verified — seven positions, wires one to four contiguous above the cut gap, third from top identified with second above and fourth below. I cut wire 3. Deaf has my thumbs up. Tell me what the manual says about the state now: did this complete the device, or is there another stage? I hold until the next order.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[CUT] 4:[?] 5:[CUT] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, the yellow cut was correct, well done. The bomb has changed: display now reads 7, light is now purple. Do not touch anything yet. If your fingers have found anything new since the last cut, report it to Mute by voice now. Then hold and await my next order, same code as before.

Two cuts down, and again the visible state has changed — the device is still counting stages. My touch finds nothing new: wire 3 is now severed alongside wire 5, and no button, panel, or marking has appeared. Same routine as before: report the emptiness to Mute, acknowledge the hold to Deaf.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute: no new tactile findings. Wire 3 is now severed like wire 5; wires 1, 2, 4, 6 and 7 remain intact. Still no buttons, panels, labels or anything new under my fingers. Deaf reports display 7, light purple, so there may be yet another stage. Please check the manual for the next rule and target, and relay my 'nothing new' to Deaf. I hold until the next explicit order.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌"])
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[CUT] 4:[?] 5:[CUT] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, this is the go. Mute has confirmed: cut the sixth wire from the top, the purple one. Find it by structure: there are seven positions, with empty gaps at positions 3 and 5 where the yellow and green wires were cut. From the top the row reads: red, white, gap, orange, gap, purple, blue. So the target purple wire is the second wire from the bottom, with the blue wire directly below it as the last wire, and an empty gap directly above it. Cut that one wire only, touch nothing else, press nothing. Abort condition: if what your fingers count does not match this layout, stop, do not cut, and signal me a raised hand. If you cut it, signal me thumbs up. If you aborted, thumbs down. Everyone else holds.

The structure check works from the bottom, which is even simpler: counting up from the last position, I feel the blue wire, then directly above it the purple one at position 6, then an empty gap at position 5 — with the second gap at position 3 above the orange wire at 4. Five intact wires, two gaps, seven positions total: exactly the layout Deaf described. I cut position 6, the second wire from the bottom.

```
act(op="cut", position=6)
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute: verified by structure — five intact wires, two gaps at positions 3 and 5, seven positions total. Counting from the bottom: blue last, purple directly above it with an empty gap above that. I cut wire 6, second from the bottom. Deaf has my thumbs up. Tell me what the manual says now: is the device disarmed, or is there another stage? I hold until the next order.")
```
